abstract.p: Autonomous agents have become increasingly promising for interacting with the real world. Android systems are widely adopted for mobile interactions, but existing studies for training and evaluating Android agents lack systematic research for both open and closed-source models. In this work, we present ANDROID-LAB as a systematic framework for building Android agents. It provides an operation environment with different modalities and a reproducible benchmark. It supports both large language models (LLMs) and vision language models (VLMs) in the same action space. The ANDROIDLAB benchmark includes predefined Android virtual devices and 138 tasks across nine Apps. By using the ANDROIDLAB environment, we develop an Android Instruction dataset and evaluate its effectiveness on six open LLMs and VLMs. The results show that the data helps increase the average success rate from 4.59% to 21.50% for LLMs, and from 1.93% to 13.28% for VLMs. ANDROID-LAB is open-sourced and publicly available at https://github.com/THUDM/Android-Lab.
